title: China’s Xu Mengtao defends Olympic aerials crown, Team USA’s Kaila Kuhn fifth
content:
LIVIGNO — Kaila Kuhn didn’t mince words. Typically, you hear Olympians offer up standard platitudes when coming short of the podium. Not Kuhn.

“I’m upset I didn’t medal,” the 22-year-old defending world champion said Wednesday, standing at the foot of the freeski aerials course in Livigno, her eyes averted from the medal stand being assembled behind her.

A familiar face was soon on top of that podium. China’s Xu Mengtao defended the gold medal she won in Beijing with a winning score of 112.90 in the competition’s one-jump-to-win finale, becoming the first athlete to win two aerials Olympic golds. Xu, 35, making her fifth Olympic appearance, earned China its second gold medal of these Games and ninth overall.

Danielle Scott earned Australia its sixth medal of these Games with silver, making Milan Cortina the country’s most successful Winter Olympics. While China’s Shao Qi joined Xu on the podium with bronze.

As for Kuhn, having made the transition from double to triple flips over the course of the last two years, the Boyne City, Mich., native went all out for her chance at gold. On her final jump, Kuhn went with a back-full-full-full, which translates to three backflips with a full twist (360 degrees) in each flip. The jump was clean, the flips were spot on, but Kuhn couldn’t stick the landing, instead smacking her face on her knee in the landing. Her score of 99.16 finished fifth, a slight improvement on her eighth-place finish four years ago.

“Having that world championships title is amazing, but this is a different event,” Kuhn said. “I’m going for a different title.”

Winter Vinecki, a 27-year-old with 11 years of experience on the U.S. freeski team, and a lengthy athletic resume as a triathlete and marathon runner, finished sixth among the six skiers to qualify for the super final.

The day began with 25 in the competition who all had an unexpected extra day to wait. Women’s aerials were supposed to be held on Tuesday in Livigno, but were pushed back 24 hours due to heavy snow in the area.

American Tasia Tanner made it out of the qualifying cut from 25 to 12, but couldn’t make it through to finals. The 23-year-old was making her Olympic debut, but said this might also be her last. She’s considering retirement following a lengthy string of injuries. “My body has been through enough,” Tanner said.
